Your wristpad lets you channel schematics into functioning tech powers (see chapter 10 for general techcasting rules and chapter 12 for the tech powers list).

Tech Powers Known. You begin knowing 3 tech powers of your choice, learning more at higher levels per the Tech Powers Known column of the Industrial Approach Techcasting table. You can't learn a power above your current Max Power Level.

Tech Points. You have a pool of tech points, spent to cast your powers, equal to half your berserker level (per the Tech Points column of the Industrial Approach Techcasting table) plus your Intelligence modifier. This pool refills after a short or long rest.

Max Power Level. Some tech powers can be overcharged for a stronger effect at greater tech point cost; the highest level you can overcharge to rises with your levels, per the Max Power Level column of the Industrial Approach Techcasting table. You may cast a power at 4th level only once between long rests, regaining that ability after finishing one.

Techcasting Ability. Intelligence governs your tech powers — you use it whenever a power calls for your techcasting ability, including setting its save DC and attack rolls.

Tech save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Tech attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Techcasting Focus. You use a wristpad (see chapter 5 of the Player's Handbook) as your focus for tech powers.
